result:
I fixed 12 rules in `pricebook.py` that didn't match their docstrings. Afterwards I checked all 150 rules against their docstrings, using quantities 0–129 plus 500, 1000 and 5000 with several unit prices. Every result matched.

| Rule | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 11 | `qty > 12`, so 12 units got no discount | `>= 12` |
| 91 | `qty >= 13` | `>= 12` |
| 119 | `qty >= 31` | `>= 30` |
| 127 | `qty > 30` | `>= 30` |
| 15 | `qty > 100` (same results, since the discount is 0 at exactly 100) | `>= 100`, to match the other rules |
| 18 | The 100,000 won cap only applied once the discount went over 200,000 | Always cap at 100,000 |
| 28 | A "whole" rule was calculated as "marginal" | Calculated on the full price (`base * 5 // 100`) |
| 44, 79, 139 | Discount was rounded with `round` | Rounded down to the won (`// 100`) |
| 65 | The cap was applied to the price instead of the discount | Calculate the discount, then cap it at 30,000 |
| 105 | Rate was 9% | 8%, as the docstring says |

Some other rules are written differently (`not qty < N`, `12 <= qty`, `if disc > cap`, `(qty * unit)`), but they give the same results, so I left them alone.

STATUS: DONE
